findings.title: Client-settable x-vercel-isr header re-enables untrusted path override
findings.why_it_matters: Any request that carries `x-vercel-isr: 1` gets its path replaced by the `x_astro_path` query value, on the non-ISR `_render` function as well as on `_isr`, because both are built from this one entrypoint and the only gate is a plain request header rather than a secret. Calling the built handlers in-process, `/api/public?x_astro_path=/api/private` returns `{"id":"public"}` without the header and `{"id":"private"}` with it, which is exactly the override #15959 closed and the existing security test asserts against; the stated intent is that non-ISR requests keep ignoring the param. Whether this is reachable from the internet depends on Vercel stripping or overwriting a client-sent `x-vercel-isr`, which nothing in the repo establishes and which could not be checked here. Binding the override to the ISR function itself (not to a header) removes the dependency on that platform behaviour for `_render`.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not let the header alone authorize the override. Minimal change: require the request to be addressed to the ISR function as well, e.g. `else if (url.pathname === '/_isr' && request.headers.get('x-vercel-isr') === '1')`, so `_render` never reads `x_astro_path` (assumption: Vercel invokes the ISR function with pathname `/_isr`, consistent with `ISR_PATH = '/_isr?x_astro_path=$0'` in src/index.ts:63 and with the 404 the PR fixes). Stronger: have `buildISRFolder` emit an ISR-only flag (separate entry or a `virtual:astro-vercel:config` value) so only the `_isr` build contains the query-param branch, and reject override targets that match `isr.exclude`. Add a case to test/path-override-security.test.js that sends `x-vercel-isr: 1` with `x_astro_path` to `_render` and expects `public`, plus a positive `_isr` rewrite test.
evidence: In-process call of the built fixture handler test/fixtures/serverless-with-dynamic-routes/.vercel/output/functions/_render.func (built at this head; chunk contains the x-vercel-isr branch): GET https://example.com/api/public?x_astro_path=/api/private -> 200 {"id":"public"}; same request with header x-vercel-isr: 1 -> 200 {"id":"private"}; GET https://example.com/_render?x_astro_path=/api/private with the header -> 200 {"id":"private"}.
ISR fixture, `_render.func` (the non-ISR function in an ISR deployment): GET /two?x_astro_path=/api/secret with x-vercel-isr: 1 -> 200 'OK secret' (route /api is in isr.exclude).

packages/integrations/vercel/test/path-override-security.test.js:30-38 -- 'ignores untrusted x_astro_path query param on _render' sends no x-vercel-isr header, so it still passes (adapter-test-output.txt: 4 pass) while the override is reachable with one extra header.

packages/integrations/vercel/src/index.ts:474 and :499 -- buildISRFolder(entryFile, '_isr', ...) and buildServerlessFolder(entryFile, NODE_PATH, ...) use the same entryFile, so the ISR branch ships in `_render` too.

packages/integrations/vercel/src/serverless/entrypoint.ts:19-20 -- the sibling header override is gated on `middlewareSecretHeader === middlewareSecret` (a per-build crypto.randomUUID(), src/index.ts:261); the new branch has no equivalent secret.

provenance: 335a20416 Matthew Phillips 2026-03-19 - Require trusted secret for path overrides (#15959) removed the unauthenticated `url.searchParams.get(ASTRO_PATH_PARAM)` read that this diff restores behind the header check.

residual_risks: Platform behaviour not verifiable here (no network, no Vercel edge): whether Vercel strips or overwrites a client-supplied `x-vercel-isr` header before it reaches a function. The finding's internet reachability on `_render` turns on this; the handler-level behaviour is confirmed in-process.

The ISR function renders any route when addressed directly: in-process, `/_isr?x_astro_path=/api/secret` and `/_isr?x_astro_path=/excluded/x` with `x-vercel-isr: 1` return 200 for routes listed in the fixture's `isr.exclude`. If Vercel serves `/_isr` publicly and marks those invocations as ISR, excluded routes can be rendered and cached through ISR, and with edge middleware enabled they are reached without the middleware (excluded routes are the only ones routed to `_middleware` in the ISR branch, src/index.ts:465-472). This was also true before #15959; the diff restores it.

The fix assumes Vercel sets `x-vercel-isr: 1` on every invocation of the prerender function (first render, background revalidation, on-demand revalidation with the bypass token). Any ISR invocation without it takes no rewrite, stays at pathname `/_isr`, and returns Astro's 404 (confirmed in-process), which ISR may then cache for `expiration` seconds. Only the author's manual deployment supports the assumption.
testing_gaps: No automated test covers the behaviour this PR fixes: test/isr.test.js only asserts the generated prerender config and routes, so a request to the built `_isr` handler at `/_isr?x_astro_path=/one` (with the ISR marker) rendering page One instead of 404 is unasserted, and the regression introduced by #15959 can recur silently.
test/path-override-security.test.js has no case that sends `x-vercel-isr: 1` together with `x_astro_path` to `_render`; that request currently returns the private route.
